## Overview

RDFLib.jl includes a built-in SPARQL server similar to Apache Jena Fuseki. It exposes RDF datasets over HTTP with support for the SPARQL Protocol, Graph Store Protocol, N3 reasoning, SHACL validation, and Jelly binary endpoints.

```{julia}
using RDFLib
```

## Creating a Server

Create a `SparqlServer` and add datasets to it.

```{julia}
# Create a server on a given port
server = SparqlServer(; port=3331, verbose=false)
println("Server created: ", typeof(server))
```

## Adding Datasets

Each dataset is an independent RDF store with its own endpoints.

```{julia}
# Add a dataset — creates a MemoryStore-backed graph by default
add_dataset!(server, "people")

# Add data to the dataset
ds = get_dataset(server, "people")
g = ds.graph
ex = Namespace("http://example.org/")
foaf = Namespace("http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/")
bind!(g, "ex", ex)
bind!(g, "foaf", foaf)

add!(g, Triple(ex("alice"), RDF.type, foaf("Person")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("alice"), foaf("name"), Literal("Alice")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("alice"), foaf("age"), Literal(30)))
add!(g, Triple(ex("alice"), foaf("knows"), ex("bob")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("bob"), RDF.type, foaf("Person")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("bob"), foaf("name"), Literal("Bob")))
add!(g, Triple(ex("bob"), foaf("age"), Literal(25)))

println("Dataset 'people' has $(length(g)) triples")
```

## Starting the Server

Start the server in the background so it runs alongside your Julia session.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# Start in background mode (non-blocking)
serve!(server; background=true)
println("Server running at http://localhost:3331")

# The server is now accepting HTTP requests
```

## SPARQL Protocol

The SPARQL endpoint accepts queries via GET or POST at `/<dataset>/sparql`.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# Query via HTTP (using curl as an example)
# GET request with query parameter:
#   curl "http://localhost:3331/people/sparql?query=SELECT+*+WHERE+{+?s+?p+?o+}+LIMIT+5"

# POST request with query in body:
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/people/sparql \
#        -H "Content-Type: application/sparql-query" \
#        -d "SELECT ?name WHERE { ?s <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/name> ?name }"

# Accept different result formats:
#   curl -H "Accept: application/sparql-results+json" \
#        "http://localhost:3331/people/sparql?query=SELECT+?s+WHERE+{+?s+?p+?o+}"
```

## SPARQL Update Endpoint

Send SPARQL UPDATE operations to `/<dataset>/update`.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# Insert new data via SPARQL Update
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/people/update \
#        -H "Content-Type: application/sparql-update" \
#        -d "INSERT DATA {
#              <http://example.org/carol> a <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/Person> ;
#                <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/name> \"Carol\" .
#            }"

# Delete data
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/people/update \
#        -H "Content-Type: application/sparql-update" \
#        -d "DELETE WHERE { <http://example.org/bob> ?p ?o }"
```

## Graph Store Protocol

The data endpoint at `/<dataset>/data` supports the W3C Graph Store Protocol for managing RDF graphs directly.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# GET — retrieve the default graph as Turtle
#   curl http://localhost:3331/people/data

# PUT — replace the entire graph
#   curl -X PUT http://localhost:3331/people/data \
#        -H "Content-Type: text/turtle" \
#        --data-binary @mydata.ttl

# POST — add triples to the graph
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/people/data \
#        -H "Content-Type: application/n-triples" \
#        --data-binary @additional.nt

# DELETE — clear the graph
#   curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3331/people/data
```

## File Upload

Upload RDF files in any supported format, including Jelly binary.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# Upload a Turtle file
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/people/upload \
#        -F "file=@data.ttl;type=text/turtle"

# Upload a Jelly binary file
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/people/upload \
#        -F "file=@data.jelly;type=application/x-jelly-rdf"
```

## N3 Reasoning Endpoint

Submit N3 rules for forward-chaining reasoning at `/<dataset>/reason`.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# Apply N3 inference rules
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/people/reason \
#        -H "Content-Type: text/n3" \
#        -d '@prefix foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/> .
#            { ?a foaf:knows ?b } => { ?b foaf:knows ?a } .'
```

## SHACL Validation Endpoint

Validate the dataset against SHACL shapes at `/<dataset>/shacl`.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# Validate against SHACL shapes
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/people/shacl \
#        -H "Content-Type: text/turtle" \
#        -d '@prefix sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
#            @prefix foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/> .
#            @prefix ex: <http://example.org/> .
#
#            ex:PersonShape a sh:NodeShape ;
#                sh:targetClass foaf:Person ;
#                sh:property [
#                    sh:path foaf:name ;
#                    sh:minCount 1 ;
#                    sh:datatype xsd:string ;
#                ] .'
```

## Jelly Binary Endpoint

The server supports Jelly as a content type for high-performance data exchange.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# Request data in Jelly format
#   curl -H "Accept: application/x-jelly-rdf" \
#        http://localhost:3331/people/data -o output.jelly

# Upload data in Jelly format
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/people/data \
#        -H "Content-Type: application/x-jelly-rdf" \
#        --data-binary @input.jelly
```

## Admin Endpoints

Manage the server and its datasets via admin endpoints under `/$`.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# Server info
#   curl http://localhost:3331/$/server

# List all datasets
#   curl http://localhost:3331/$/datasets

# Create a new dataset
#   curl -X POST http://localhost:3331/$/datasets \
#        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
#        -d '{"name": "newdata"}'

# Delete a dataset
#   curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3331/$/datasets/people

# Health check
#   curl http://localhost:3331/$/ping
```

## Programmatic Client Usage

You can also interact with the server from Julia using HTTP.jl.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using HTTP

# Query the server programmatically
query = "SELECT ?name WHERE { ?s <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/name> ?name }"
resp = HTTP.get("http://localhost:3331/people/sparql";
    query=Dict("query" => query),
    headers=Dict("Accept" => "application/sparql-results+json"))
println(String(resp.body))
```

## Stopping the Server

```{julia}
#| eval: false
stop!(server)
println("Server stopped")
```

## Summary

| Endpoint | Method | Path | Description |
|----------|--------|------|-------------|
| SPARQL Query | GET/POST | `/<ds>/sparql` | Run SPARQL queries |
| SPARQL Update | POST | `/<ds>/update` | Run SPARQL updates |
| Graph Store | GET/PUT/POST/DELETE | `/<ds>/data` | Manage graph data |
| File Upload | POST | `/<ds>/upload` | Upload RDF files |
| N3 Reasoning | POST | `/<ds>/reason` | Apply inference rules |
| SHACL Validation | POST | `/<ds>/shacl` | Validate shapes |
| Server Info | GET | `/$/server` | Server metadata |
| List Datasets | GET | `/$/datasets` | List datasets |
| Create Dataset | POST | `/$/datasets` | Add dataset |
| Delete Dataset | DELETE | `/$/datasets/<ds>` | Remove dataset |
| Health Check | GET | `/$/ping` | Ping |
